relations: The existing raspberry pile on the tart persists as the landing target for berries descending from above.
Falling berries enter at the top edge and move downward in separate staggered paths toward the tart.
The loose table berries, flour bowl, and background bowl remain stationary while new berries descend.
Several berries stay in mid-air above the plate at the end, so the topping is not finalized.
caption:
The video captures a bright, shallow-depth kitchen tabletop still life centered on a wedge of pink raspberry meringue tart resting on a small white plate. A clear glass bowl of flour sits blurred in the left foreground, while a white bowl of raspberries fills the background and a few loose berries lie on the table at the right. The tart carries a small pile of red raspberries, and that pile remains visible as additional berries begin to fall. From the top edge, raspberries enter and move downward in staggered paths toward the dessert.

More berries appear at the top and descend steadily in front of the background bowl, moving just above the tart while still in the air. The falling sequence remains one berry after another rather than a single mass, and the loose berries, flour bowl, and background bowl are not seen moving independently. Several raspberries remain in motion above the plate at the end, so the topping is not shown settling into a final, completed, stable state.
